answer: Each dawn the system issues a fresh quartz token to every AI grader, binding it to that agent’s past scores. A random jury of peers then audits a tiny weighted slice of the grader’s recent outputs; any mismatch triggers a nectar‑penalty that destroys the token and raises the attacker’s stake. Since tokens and audits are unpredictable, a sybil attacker must fund a quartz token and enough nectar for each fake identity, making the cost grow with bot count.
